solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Astute Kate maybe seen with daughter

parts.note: Kate is the title character of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew; 'maybe' marks her as an example
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone called Kate is admired for her sharpness when she appears alongside her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate (Katherina) is the headstrong heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, so she is a SHREW; add D to get SHREWD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd is a direct synonym of astute: clever and sharp in judging situations.

clue.text: Matching collection in place for filming

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of things that belong together, like a tea service
second meaning: the constructed scenery where a film is shot

explanation.surface: A coordinated set of props is positioned where a film is being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The same short word names both a matched group of items and a film studio's built scenery.

clue.text: Stood as candidate over ruler's position

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to run for office is to stand as a candidate
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone contested an election to gain a monarch's status.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a place or standing in a graded order, so it is a position.

clue.text: Been changed with water, heat? Becoming this maybe

definitions.text: Been changed with water, heat? Becoming this maybe

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something exposed to rain and sun ends up looking battered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: anything long exposed to water and heat may become weather-beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather-beaten describes something worn and damaged by prolonged exposure to wind, rain and sun.

clue.text: Protective cover of cab up for alteration after hours

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hours

indicators.note: letters put up for alteration are to be changed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxi's protective cover goes in for repair once the working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after hours' places the H in front of the rearranged letters, giving HUBCAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hubcap is the metal disc fitted over a car wheel's hub to shield it.

clue.text: Unexpected turn — gear ad due to show student

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out differently from usual, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprise development: an advert for equipment is set to feature a student.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student working towards a first degree.

clue.text: Covered by article, a number with no record of offences

indicators.note: something covered by other words lies inside them, concealed across their letters

parts.note: found running across the end of article, a, and the start of number

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reports that a certain number of people have no criminal history.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a clean record has no convictions, so clean means free of offences.

clue.text: Press on agent after return, strict

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the agent's word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
severe means strict or harsh

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to keep going once a stern agent comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist despite difficulty, which is to press on.

clue.text: Pacific kingdom not backing limits on Georgia

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two end letters, the only ones kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Georgia

explanation.surface: A Pacific nation declines to support restrictions placed on the state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island monarchy in the South Pacific, the only remaining kingdom in Polynesia.

clue.text: June, July maybe? I'm ready afresh

indicators.note: doing something afresh means making it anew, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are ready again for the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags June and July as examples of the definition rather than its full meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: June and July fall in the middle of the calendar, so they are examples of midyear months.

clue.text: Turning up on regular basis, Kantism provides valuable material

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means flipping upward, so the letters are read in reverse
doing something on a regular basis means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A philosophy student finds Kant's thought keeps proving precious when it comes up regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kantism is the philosophy of Immanuel Kant; only its alternate letters matter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mink is a costly fur, so it is a valuable material for coats.

clue.text: Page greeting character from Athens

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A page boy says hello to a visitor from the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' here means a letter of an alphabet, and Athens points to Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens.

clue.text: Sensible pal welcoming Catholic who's penned Act One

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the friend's word takes the rest inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to have penned something is to have shut it in, as in a pen, so the Catholic abbreviation encloses what follows

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Act One written as ACT plus the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A level-headed friend hosts a Catholic playwright who has just finished the first act.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'penned' is read as enclosed rather than written, so the Catholic abbreviation holds Act One, and that sits inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical means sensible and realistic, concerned with what actually works.

clue.text: Back, having managed Church, seeing obstacle to progress

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs
ran means managed, as one runs a business
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone returns after running a church and finds their way forward blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that impedes or holds back advancement, a close synonym.

clue.text: Wretched rag? No! A valued wool

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry state, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a fine woollen garment is not a miserable rag at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is soft, prized fibre from Angora rabbits or goats, a costly kind of wool.

clue.text: Resentful feeling after long walk, briefly good for time at start

indicators.note: one thing stands in for another, here replacing the opening letter that stands for time

parts.note: a trudge is a long weary walk
G is the short form of good
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: After a tiring hike someone is left with a sour feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the front of TRUDGE is swapped for G, giving GRUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge is a lasting sense of ill will or resentment towards someone.

clue.text: Figure involved in Media Monday

indicators.note: something involved in a phrase is caught up inside it, lying across its words

parts.note: found running from the end of media into the start of Monday

explanation.surface: A public figure features in the media at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' invites a person; here it means a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is a rhombus, a four-sided shape, so it is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Success — a learner's tap-in maybe

parts.note: as in 'make a go of it', meaning succeed
taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A novice footballer celebrates scoring with a simple tap-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Success' looks like the definition but supplies the first piece; the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-in is an easy goal scored from very close range, so it is one example.

clue.text: Instructed to include ultimately rough sandbank in triplicate?

indicators.note: one word is made to include others, wrapping around them

parts.note: to be told is to be instructed

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of rough
a reef is a ridge of sand or rock near the surface

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put the rough sandbank in their report three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instructed' looks like the definition's verb, but the definition is the closing phrase; the question mark admits that threefold only loosely means in triplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Threefold means three times over, and in triplicate means in three copies, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Referring to Kitty, put plant in new container

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
a kitty is a pot of pooled money

explanation.surface: Talking about a cat named Kitty, someone moves a houseplant into a bigger pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat's name, but it is the pool of money in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to transfer a plant into a fresh or larger pot.

clue.text: Cut initially announced by English

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letters of the words that follow are taken

parts.note: the first letter of announced
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in measurements like 3 x 4
the first letter of English

explanation.surface: A cutback is first made public by an English authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' = X comes from dimensions such as 'two by four', written 2 x 4.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut, especially to cut jobs or spending abruptly.

clue.text: Paris or Rome? Excellent!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a city that is a seat of national government, Paris and Rome being examples
second meaning: an old-fashioned British exclamation of approval

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a European city and is congratulated on the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' is a dated British way of saying 'splendid!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris and Rome are national seats of government; 'capital' also serves as an exclamation meaning first-rate.

clue.text: Happening at the outset, attractive feature of our times

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so each following word gives just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Something attractive is said to be a hallmark of the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means under way or in progress, as in 'something is afoot'.

clue.text: Hill rubbish must be tipped

indicators.note: tipping something up in a down clue inverts it, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Waste on a hillside has to be dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky peak or hill, especially in the West Country of England.

clue.text: Literature no matter what? It could be repetitive

parts.note: lit is a short form of literature, as in English lit
any as in 'any one will do', whichever it is

explanation.surface: A reader asks whether any book will do, worrying it might all be the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: a litany is a long recital with repeated responses.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of prayers with repeated responses, or by extension any tediously repeated list.

clue.text: Information linked to the German grammatical category

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
der is the German masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Data is tied to a classification found in German grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British English for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is the grammatical class of nouns, such as masculine, feminine or neuter, as in German.
